cohort: Pregnant patients with serologically confirmed dengue fever (n=24) compared with an age-matched group of healthy pregnant mothers without symptomatic dengue illness (n=72).
finding: There were no statistically significant differences in birth weight, prematurity, or peripartum complications between the dengue-exposed and unexposed groups, however, neonates born to mothers with dengue infection needed more PBU admissions and a longer hospital stay.
